links.outcome: Association of assessment errors with sociodemographic and linguistic variables and symptom severity
links.effect: Most variables showed minimal association with errors; higher depression and anxiety severity linked to larger absolute errors (β = .193, p = .038; β = .252, p = .003).
links.quote: Our analysis revealed limited evidence of demographic or linguistic bias: most variables showed minimal association with assessment errors (i.e., the absolute differences between the LBAs and self reports).

links.outcome: Effect of downsampling training data on severity-related bias
links.effect: Downsampling training data eliminated the bias for depression and anxiety.
links.quote: We explored mitigation strategies, finding that downsampling training data eliminated the bias for depression and anxiety.
